title: Germany news: Merz hopes for Korean reunification at DMZ
summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz has expressed hope for Korean reunification during a visit to the heavily fortified border. Meanwhile, President Steinmeier has held talks with China's Xi Jinping in…
byline: Richard Connor, Matt Ford, Wesley Rahn, Alex Berry

image.caption: South Korea is the final stop on Merz's five-day Asia tour, following visits to Singapore and JapanImage: Kay Nietfeld/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Merz at DMZ says he hopes Korea can reunify like Germany did

blocks.caption: Merz visited the "T2" barrack building at the DMZImage: Kay Nietfeld/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Friday visited the Panmunjom truce village at the demilitarized zone (DMZ) separating North and South Korea, briefly standing on the North Korean side inside the barracks.
North and South Korea have been divided since the end of hostilities in the Korean War in 1953, with a border running across the peninsula.

blocks.caption: Merz briefly stepped into the 'North Korean side' behind a conference table in the border barrack buildingImage: Kay Nietfeld/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: In remarks to reporters, Merz recalled Germany's reunification 36 years ago.
"Let us hope that Korea too gets the chance one day to regain state unity," he said.

"You can also notice it here at this place, how much a country suffers from division and how strong the desire is for reunification, at least in this part of the Korean Peninsula," he said, adding that he had been asked about Germany's reunification experience while visiting Seoul.

North Korea, however, has backed away in recent years from diplomacy with the South, having officially removed language calling for reunification from its constitution while changing the South's status to that of a "hostile state."
